context_requirements: Functional AVPR2 (or AVPR1A/AVPR1B/OXTR) expression on the cell line; AVPR2 is the main receptor mediating cAMP/PKA and PI3K/AKT signaling in responsive tumor cells
Intact cAMP/PKA and PI3K/AKT signaling downstream of the receptor
Tumor cells dependent on vasopressin/AVPR2 autocrine or paracrine signaling for proliferation and survival

Response is expected to be weak and slow in most lines because vasopressin receptor expression is low in many of the nine lines and the primary effect is antiproliferative rather than directly transcriptional
falsifiers: No reduction in proliferation-associated landmark genes (e.g., CCND1, MYC, PCNA, MKI67, CDK1, TOP2A) at 24 h in any line
No increase in CDKN1A or other cell-cycle arrest markers at 24 h
No change in cAMP/PKA or PI3K/AKT pathway readouts at either time point
Strong and rapid (6 h) transcriptional changes in lines lacking AVPR2/AVPR1A/AVPR1B/OXTR expression
Transcriptional response indistinguishable from vehicle across all nine lines at both 6 h and 24 h

evidence.supports: Tolvaptan, an AVPR2 antagonist, reduces tumor growth in a SCLC xenograft, inhibits cAMP/PKA and PI3K/AKT signaling, lowers PCNA and increases caspase-3, supporting antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects of vasopressin receptor antagonism.
Tolvaptan has antiproliferative effects in human SCLC cells and modulates cell cycle, apoptosis, oxidative stress and invasivity, supporting a slow antiproliferative transcriptional response.

The vasopressin receptor antagonist mozavaptan was used in PKD mice and kidney transcriptional profiles were evaluated, supporting that vasopressin receptor antagonism can alter transcriptional programs in responsive tissue.
